sentence: This project collects, stores and shares tissue samples from ovarian cancer patients and builds tumor models from patient samples for early lab tests.
This project builds iron-sensitive MRI scans that can tell apart types of frontotemporal lobar degeneration in living patients.
This project supports clinical research on tuberculosis by offering advice and access to patient cohorts, datasets and samples.
This project tests whether antibodies that enter cells and bind nucleic acids can carry drugs into glioblastoma and help the immune system attack it.
This project studies how key synapse proteins behave in health and disease, using genetics, live animal imaging, biochemistry and physiology.
This project looks for causes of cancer, tests natural compounds and vaccines against it, and develops biomarkers and imaging to find cancer early.
This project develops heart MRI methods for a wide-bore, low-field machine so that patients with severe obesity can get clear heart images.
This project studies how stem cells rebuild the trabecular meshwork of the eye, a tissue that helps control pressure inside the eye.
This project tries to find out how a gene rearrangement causes acute myeloid leukemia, using genetic, proteomic and drug-based methods.
This project studies how a protein called anoctamin 6 lets cancer-associated fibroblasts feed and protect pancreatic tumor cells, and whether blocking it helps.
This project develops a form of digoxin that switches on only inside irradiated tumors, testing it in medulloblastoma with organoids and animals.
This project develops a mind-body treatment to help adults with serious mental illness stop smoking cigarettes.
This project develops a faster way to collect deuterium metabolic imaging and MRI scans together so patients need less time in the scanner.
This project studies the protein systems that carry nutrients across the cell envelope of the bacterium that causes tuberculosis.
This project studies how intestinal stem cells sense damage in the gut and steer immune responses against infection and chronic inflammation.
This project develops a lab process to make red blood cells from stem cells for tests that find antibodies in people needing transfusion.
This project studies how blocking a signaling molecule helps T cells fight cancer, and tests compounds that turn this signal up or down.
This project studies how a host protein helps coronaviruses multiply and cause severe COVID-19, and whether it could guide treatment.
This project develops treatments that restore normal mitochondrial function in cocaine use disorder, testing them in awake mice with fluorescent sensors.
This project develops blood and urine tests that predict which people will develop late radiation injury in the lung and kidney after radiation exposure.
